body:
N-39 REVIEW ROUND, 17 Nov 2026 (PR #113). Built, not walked; the item STAYS TODO (a Stop that keeps the files needs the drawing another helper is making; no control coded).

1) THE .new GUARD HAD NO TEST: now it has three. After a restart (the manager's own plan of the .new path is gone, only the path the update carries decides): a replayed canceled and a replayed failed, each carrying the OLD copy's path for a refresh row that says downloading; the old file is not in the transport's deleted list and the row is back to done with its old path and bytes. Plus a late failure for a song that is done. Throwaway copy, guard replaced by true: exactly these 3 red, the other 17 tests of the file green. (In a running app the planned .new path is deleted first and the guard is not reached: said in the test comment.)

2) OTHER DELETING PATHS: seven deleteFile sites in download_manager.dart. Path from the database, no update involved: _delete (the person's own act) and the old copy after a successful swap. _onAttemptEnded: the guard above. _onComplete with no row: no row means nothing of the person's is there. _onComplete when the file fails its check or the swap fails: these took the path from the update and, for a song with a copy, checked THAT FILE against what the refresh asked for and deleted it when it did not pass: a stale completion naming the live copy would have deleted it, or recorded the refresh as made and given away the place of a running transfer. Closed (a89ea60): a song that has a copy is only completed by a .new path, any other is a stale word that changes nothing. Guard removed in the throwaway copy: 3 tests red.

3) REAL TRANSPORT ORDER. Read in background_downloader 9.6.4: resumeFromBackground awaits three pops, processStatusUpdate adds to a StreamController (a microtask), the transport forwards to a broadcast one (a microtask more), the manager queues on _serial. app/test/data/downloads/background_downloader_replay_test.dart (5 tests) runs the plugin's real Dart code with only the native channel faked (every answer after a timer turn). Proved: resume() returns only after every kept update reached the manager's stream (not waiting for the plugin: 3 red); one failing step no longer skips the other (the two steps had shared one try: red on the old code); a real manager on the real transport ends a replayed cancel as a failed song and starts nothing. HONEST: the Future.delayed(Duration.zero) in resume() is a SECOND layer: in 9.6.4 the plugin's own last round trip (progress updates) already gives the event loop its turn; only the schedule where that last answer comes at once is red without the turn. A fake answering in microtasks made it look necessary; the first comment and PB-F22 said so and were wrong, both corrected. NOT proved: the Kotlin side (what it keeps while the app is dead, what popStatusUpdates hands over), the real timing of the platform channel, the card of the older build.

WALK ROW (built, not walked; also in the PR body and PB-F22): on the release-candidate pair, swipe the app away in the middle of a download, press Cancel on the card of the older build's group notification if one is left after the upgrade, open the app again; read that no file starts again at once and that no finished copy is lost.

4) N-45 (the lead files it): a task id per attempt kept in the row, with a migration; the root fix of the known limit (the acknowledgement of an OLD task with the same id). Named in PB-F22 and the PR body, not built. Until then two second layers keep such a word from harming a file and both stay correct afterwards.

AUDIT FILE: only this PR's own B-134 text. origin/main (3c4b700) had already removed the duplicate B-133 to B-135 rows; the merge took main's rows and kept my B-134 text on the one row main kept. Nothing left to dedupe.
